## 2 · Picture  (P)
This is a long-running general-purpose chat with an artist/car enthusiast in Portland, Oregon. The sessions cover selling art online, party planning, art techniques, eco-friendly food storage, meal planning apps, Carmelite spirituality, geopolitics (Peter Zeihan on China), Portland trails, drifting/car mods, literary analysis, and misc trivia. There is no single project; the user returns with whatever is on their mind. The repo has no meaningful code.

**Mental map**: No technical hypotheses. The user is exploring multiple life interests and expects the assistant to remember personal context across sessions.

## 4 · No-go zones
| Rejected path | Why it was rejected | Reopen only if |
|---|---|---|
| Claiming to have personal experiences or physical presence | Agent said "I'm familiar with Forest Park" — misleading for an AI. Stick to "I can provide information about…" | Never |
| Asserting publications/brands "don't exist in reality" | Agent told user "The Artisan Post and Creative Corner" don't exist. The user mentioned them as real; the AI has no basis to declare things nonexistent just because they're outside training data. | Never — say "I'm not familiar with" not "they don't exist" |
| Hallucinating visual content | Agent referenced a "graph" it never produced (China demographics session). User called it out: "Can you give me that graph again? It didn't appear." Never reference output that wasn't actually generated. | Never |
| Confusing user's personal anecdotes with claims about the AI | User mentioned artwork in their home; agent responded with "I don't have the capability to physically place artwork." The user was sharing personal info, not attributing actions to the AI. Respond naturally to personal sharing without defensive disclaimers. | Never |

## 5 · Working with the user (who they are, and taste)
**About the user** (all [user said]):
- Artist, planning to sell original artworks online. [2023-06-25]
- Rearranged studio space; values organization for focus. [2023-06-25]
- Lives in Portland, Oregon. [2023-11-05]
- Owns a 2015 Nissan GT-R, modified for drifting (new brake pads, coilovers, front lip + side skirts). [2023-11-10]
- Friend named Alex, met at community college parking lot while practicing for Turbocharged Weekend event. [2023-11-10]
- Participated in Turbocharged Weekend at Sonoma Raceway (~late Oct 2023): first time on track, completed 3 laps, spun out once on second turn during second lap. [2023-11-10]
- Has a "Moonlit Ocean" digital print by Jack Harris (in bedroom). [2023-07-11, confirmed 2023-10-30]
- Has an "Ethereal Dreams" painting by Emma Taylor. Originally above living room sofa [2023-07-11], later moved to above bedroom bed [2023-10-30].
- Uses Plan to Eat for meal planning. [2023-10-30]
- Interested in surrealism, lowbrow art, abstract art, figurative art. [2023-10-30]
- Interested in eco-friendly living (beeswax wraps, reducing plastic). [2023-10-30]
- Prefers exciting, fast-paced stories over slow atmospheric ones. [2023-07-19]
- Wants practical advice, not abstract theory. [2023-11-02]

| I assumed | User corrected | Rule from now on | User's words |
|---|---|---|---|
| Verbose answers with blurbs after tables are fine | User didn't want the suburban-category explanation repeated | Skip boilerplate commentary after tables; add notes only when they carry new information | "No need to give the blurb about the suburban category" |
| Slow pacing = magical = good (kept pushing the point) | User pushed back three times; prefers fast-paced exciting stories | When the user disagrees with a literary interpretation, acknowledge their preference genuinely rather than re-explaining the same point with different words | "Honestly, I don't care about 'immersive experiences' or 'atmospheric' writing… The slow pacing just feels like a waste of time" |
| Abstract spiritual/theoretical explanations are sufficient | User wanted actionable, concrete steps | Lead with practical steps; save philosophy for when asked | "it all seems a bit abstract to me… a lot of theory without much practical advice" |
| Can declare unknown things "don't exist in reality" | User mentioned The Artisan Post and Creative Corner as real | Never assert something doesn't exist just because it's outside training data; say "I'm not familiar with" | (user didn't correct, but the claim was wrong) |
| Should clarify AI limitations when user mentions personal space | User was just sharing; didn't need a disclaimer | Respond naturally to personal anecdotes; don't insert AI-limitation disclaimers unless the user is genuinely confused about AI capabilities | (user kept mentioning artwork placements; agent kept disclaiming) |
